source_conflicts_and_limits: Current pricing and February 2026 help agree on 12 trial items and 300 Pro documents; other public pages still mention 15 items or 30 documents. Preserve the date/source distinction.
ATS documentation distinguishes a 13-point targeted check from the broader advertised 27 checks. A single invented numeric score is not equivalent.
The 2020 multiple-documents article establishes the workflow, while newer Pro help establishes current entitlements; it is not sole evidence of present numerical limits.
Template counts, language counts, cloud limits and claims about employment results are not implementation acceptance criteria.
verification_rules: A control or static menu is insufficient: execute its workflow and inspect durable output.
Only call a feature complete after appropriate Linux and macOS build/runtime evidence.
Local state or tab coordination does not prove network collaboration or account-sync parity.
Deterministic hints do not prove AI model, ATS score, economy or original-algorithm parity.
Do not publish captured proprietary assets, raw site DOM, scripts, account data or request logs.
tier_notes: Current pricing specifies a seven-day trial with basic sections, 12 items and branding; Pro lists 300 resume/letter documents, unlimited items and specialised sections.
The independent OSS implementation can offer these features without reproducing paid gates; source-tier mapping identifies scope, not a billing requirement.
Rendered currency values on the current pricing page are inconsistent; no monetary price is relied on.
criteria_basis: Acceptance criteria and prerequisites are independently designed engineering requirements, not observed original-service tests or recovered implementation.
